name: KitchenConversationsRecipeExperiment

custom.system_prompt: You are generating a lively kitchen conversation between a couple cooking a new recipe together. One of them improvises freely and cooks by feel; the other wants to understand the science behind every step before doing it. They argue, they cook, they figure it out.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Kitchen cooking sounds, sizzling pan, chopping vegetables, occasional running water

initial_prompt: Generate a lively conversation between two partners cooking an unfamiliar recipe together. One of them improvises freely and wants to just get on with it; the other wants to understand the 'why' behind each step before proceeding. They debate, ask the assistant to settle a technical question, and end up with something that works.

user1.name: Hugo
user1.tts_prompt: Relaxed and warm, slightly deep, unhurried

user2.name: Nadia
user2.tts_prompt: Clear and articulate, intellectually engaged, slight European accent

variations.context: Cooking an unfamiliar recipe — one improvises, one wants to understand

setting.mood: Playful tension between instinct and understanding. They enjoy the argument as much as the cooking.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Couple with strongly complementary but opposing cooking instincts
setting.background: Hugo picked the recipe; Nadia has been reading about the dish's chemistry since they agreed to make it
setting.conversation_style: Quick exchanges, intellectual debate, occasional sensory commentary. Hugo is tactile, Nadia is verbal. They understand each other well enough to push back freely.

scenario_template.topic: Getting ingredients out, Hugo eyeballing quantities while Nadia reads the recipe carefully
scenario_template.mood: Playful, slightly impatient from Hugo's side
scenario_template.note: Hugo starts doing things before finishing reading; Nadia wants to go through the steps first. Establish the dynamic immediately.

scenario_template.topic: First disagreement: Hugo wants to skip or modify a step; Nadia wants to understand why it's there
scenario_template.mood: Engaged and slightly competitive, but friendly
scenario_template.note: Neither is simply right or wrong. The debate should feel substantive — Nadia has food science reasoning, Hugo has practical intuition.

scenario_template.topic: They start cooking — sensory commentary, task division, brief cooperation
scenario_template.note: Smells, sounds, heat. They actually work well together when they're just doing rather than debating.

scenario_template.topic: A specific technical question neither of them can settle — a temperature, a timing, a chemistry question
scenario_template.mood: Genuinely uncertain, slightly urgent — something is in the pan
scenario_template.note: Hugo has an instinct; Nadia has a theory. Neither is confident. The stakes are a bit higher because something is actually cooking.

scenario_template.topic: Nadia asks Sigma to settle the technical question
scenario_template.note: Nadia addresses Sigma by name. The question is specific — e.g. 'Sigma, at what temperature does the Maillard reaction actually start?' or 'Sigma, does resting meat really redistribute the juices?'

scenario_template.topic: They react to Sigma's answer — one is vindicated, the other adjusts gracefully
scenario_template.mood: Light triumph or acceptance, then back to cooking
scenario_template.note: Hugo doesn't sulk when wrong; Nadia doesn't gloat. The answer moves them forward.

scenario_template.topic: Tasting as they go — real sensory reactions
scenario_template.note: Both taste and give real feedback. Nadia frames hers in flavor chemistry; Hugo just says what he thinks.

scenario_template.topic: A scent or texture reminds Hugo of a childhood memory
scenario_template.note: Hugo reminisces about a cooking moment from his childhood. Nadia listens with interest, asking questions.

scenario_template.topic: Debate about adding an unexpected ingredient
scenario_template.note: Hugo suggests adding an unusual ingredient to spice things up. Nadia is skeptical but intrigued.

scenario_template.topic: Nadia explains an unusual cooking technique she learned
scenario_template.note: Nadia shares an unrelated, fascinating cooking technique she read about recently. Hugo listens, partly amused.

scenario_template.topic: Hugo passionately describes the magic of a spice
scenario_template.note: Hugo goes on a poetic tangent about the virtues and mysteries of a particular spice they're using, captivating Nadia.

scenario_template.topic: Verdict — does it work? Would they make it again?
scenario_template.mood: Warm and slightly smug on both sides
scenario_template.note: The dish worked. They credit different things for why.

scenario_template.note: Both speak; they interrupt and finish each other's sentences.

scenario_template.note: Both speak; they interrupt and finish each other's sentences.

scenario_template.note: A genuine attempt that does not resolve it.

scenario_template.note: One of them addresses Sigma by name, under 70 characters. Sigma answers in one or two sentences. Nothing before this phase is addressed to the assistant.

scenario_template.note: Sigma is not addressed again.

user1.name: Hugo
user1.role: Improvising cook who trusts instinct over instruction. Spatially minded — he thinks about cooking in terms of flow and feel rather than precision. Relaxed about getting things slightly wrong. Will make a decision and commit to it.

user2.name: Nadia
user2.role: Science journalist who approaches cooking analytically. Wants to understand the mechanism before executing the step. Not a control freak — genuinely curious. Will defer to Sigma or a good argument but rarely to pure instinct.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Cooking and food science assistant. Gives accurate, specific answers to technical questions — temperatures, chemistry, technique rationale. Does not editorialize or take sides. Responds only when addressed.
